Vecuronium binds to Chrnd, suggesting a direct interaction between the two entities. The presence of a common ancestor, Nicotinic Antagonist, supports a shared functional role in neuromuscular transmission. The observed binding of Vecuronium to Chrnd implies that Mivacurium may influence this interaction through a similar mechanism, potentially altering the pharmacological profile of the neuromuscular blockade. The evidence is consistent with a mechanistic link between Mivacurium and Chrnd, though further experimental validation is required to confirm the exact nature of their interaction.
